reforms.description: The federal government established the Canada Foundation for Innovation in 1997 as an arm's-length arrangement to jointly award funds with provinces and the private sector for updating research infrastructure and equipment to support state-of-the-art research.
reforms.package_name: Federal Research and Innovation Support Initiatives
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Investment in research infrastructure enhances the capacity for scientific discovery and technological development, supporting long-term productivity growth and innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: The Canada Foundation for Innovation was established in 1997 and awards funds jointly with provinces and private sector.
reforms.importance_rationale: A major structural initiative creating a dedicated, arm's-length institution for research infrastructure funding with multi-sector participation (federal, provincial, private), representing a significant system-wide commitment to modernizing Canada's research capacity.
reforms.source_quote: The Canada Foundation for Innovation, an arm's-length arrangement established in 1997 that awards funds jointly with the provinces and the private sector to update research infrastructure and equipment for state-of-the-art research.

reforms.description: The federal government introduced the Canada Research Chairs programme to attract leading researchers to Canadian universities, supporting human capital development in the research sector.
reforms.package_name: Federal Research and Innovation Support Initiatives
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Attracting world-class researchers to Canadian universities enhances research quality and productivity, generating spillovers for innovation and human capital development.
reforms.status_evidence: Canada Research Chairs is listed among recent federal government initiatives supporting research in universities.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant targeted initiative to build research human capital by attracting excellence to Canadian universities, with meaningful but narrower scope than system-wide infrastructure reform.
reforms.source_quote: Canada Research Chairs to attract the best researchers to Canadian universities

reforms.description: The federal government supported genome science centres to accelerate genome research, directing public R&D funding toward a strategic sectoral research priority.
reforms.package_name: Federal Research and Innovation Support Initiatives
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Strategic investment in genomics research supports long-term innovation in biotechnology and health sectors, with potential for significant productivity and health-related economic returns.
reforms.status_evidence: Genome science centres are listed among recent federal government initiatives supporting research.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant sectoral R&D initiative targeting a strategic research frontier (genomics), with meaningful scope but narrower than cross-cutting infrastructure or human capital reforms.
reforms.source_quote: genome science centres to accelerate genome research

reforms.description: The federal government supported PRECARN, an industry-led consortium enabling companies to undertake research in artificial intelligence, facilitating private-sector R&D in a strategic technology domain.
reforms.package_name: Federal Research and Innovation Support Initiatives
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Supporting industry-led R&D in artificial intelligence builds private-sector innovation capacity and technological capabilities in a high-value domain, supporting productivity and competitiveness.
reforms.status_evidence: PRECARN is listed among recent federal government initiatives supporting research.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant sectoral R&D initiative supporting private-sector innovation in artificial intelligence through a consortium model, with meaningful scope in a strategic technology area.
reforms.source_quote: PRECARN, an industry-led consortium to help companies undertake research in artificial intelligence

reforms.description: The federal government committed to investment in the knowledge economy through improvements to universities and research facilities, research subsidies for knowledge-based industries, and a tax deduction for post-secondary students.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Investment in universities, research facilities, and research subsidies for knowledge-based industries enhances human capital and research capacity, supporting long-term productivity and innovation-driven growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The government set its priorities for the term of office commencing November 2000 in a Four Part Plan that included investment in the knowledge economy through improvements to universities and research facilities.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant commitment to knowledge-economy investment spanning multiple instruments (university improvements, research facilities, research subsidies, and tax incentives for post-secondary education), reflecting a broad policy shift toward innovation-driven growth.
reforms.source_quote: Investment in the knowledge economy will come from improvements to universities and research facilities, research subsidies for knowledge-based industries and a tax deduction for post-secondary students.

reforms.description: Canada adopted a new Science and Technology Strategy (1994) repositioning government from picking 'winners' to acting as a catalyst, creating partnerships and arm's-length agencies to deliver R&D spending, with the goal of ranking in the top five countries for R&D performance by 2010 by more than doubling R&D expenditures.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Doubling R&D expenditures and repositioning government as a catalyst for innovation partnerships aims to address Canada's 'innovation gap' and improve productivity performance, which are key drivers of long-term GDP growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'In 1994, the government had launched a wholesale policy review and repositioned its policies in a new Science and Technology Strategy' and describes the strategy's ongoing implementation.
reforms.importance_rationale: This is a system-wide strategic repositioning of Canada's entire R&D policy framework, moving from direct government intervention to a catalyst model and setting an ambitious national goal to double R&D expenditures and rank in the top five OECD countries by 2010. It represents a fundamental shift in innovation governance and has broad, persistent implications for the entire research ecosystem.
reforms.source_quote: In 1994, the government had launched a wholesale policy review and repositioned its policies in a new Science and Technology Strategy... the government vacated the role of a prime mover trying to pick 'winners' and instead become a catalyst, creating partnerships or arm's-length agencies to deliver R&D spending.

reforms.description: The federal government created arm's-length agencies and foundations to deliver R&D, partnering with the private sector, other government levels, universities and research agencies to optimize public-sector investment in research and development.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Arm's-length governance of R&D aims to limit political influence on research selection and overcome private-sector undervaluation of long-term research benefits, potentially improving productivity-enhancing investment allocation.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'The federal government has embarked on a strategy for optimising public-sector investment by creating partnerships with the private sector, other levels of government, universities and research agencies and creating arm's-length agencies to deliver R&D.'
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant structural reform to R&D governance and funding delivery through arm's-length institutions, addressing Canada's low R&D investment relative to OECD peers and the US-Canada productivity gap. However, the text notes implementation challenges and lack of transparency in decision-making.
reforms.source_quote: The federal government has embarked on a strategy for optimising public-sector investment by creating partnerships with the private sector, other levels of government, universities and research agencies and creating arm's-length agencies to deliver R&D.

reforms.description: The Canada Foundation for Innovation was established as a delegated arrangement to regenerate the research capital base, operating as an independent body with discretionary authority over programme design and delivery within a strategic policy framework.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Investment in research capital infrastructure supports long-term productivity growth and innovation capacity, though effectiveness depends on clear performance measurement and accountability.
reforms.status_evidence: The Canada Foundation for Innovation is listed as an example of a delegated arrangement in Box 6 and discussed as an existing programme in the text.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant institution for research infrastructure investment, but the Auditor General noted it lacks a baseline of existing research capital to measure effectiveness, limiting its ability to demonstrate impact on productivity.
reforms.source_quote: In another example, the Canada Foundation for Innovation aims to 'regenerate the research capital base', but does not have a baseline of existing research capital to measure the effectiveness of its spending.

reforms.description: The government adopted tax changes recommended by the Canadian E-business Opportunities Roundtable to improve incentives for risk-taking in venture capital and e-commerce, including reduction in capital-gains-inclusion rate and deferral of tax on stock options and capital gains on small-firm investments.
reforms.package_name: E-business and Venture Capital Tax Incentives
reforms.component_name: Capital gains and stock option tax measures
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Reduces tax burden on risk capital and entrepreneurial compensation, improving incentives for venture investment and startup formation in technology sectors.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'some of the tax changes recommended in the Report were adopted by the government in the February 2000 Budget' and further cuts were announced in October 2000 Budget Update.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant narrower reform addressing venture capital constraints and e-business development through multiple coordinated tax instruments; part of broader effort to improve Canada's innovation ecosystem and startup competitiveness.
reforms.source_quote: Some of the tax changes recommended in the Report were adopted by the government in the February 2000 Budget. These include the reduction in the capital-gains-inclusion rate as well as the ability to defer tax on stock options of less than C$100000 and on capital gains on investments of up to C$500000.

reforms.description: The October 2000 Budget Update announced a further cut in the federal capital-gains-inclusion rate from 67 to 50 per cent, and accelerated the timetable for reducing the corporate tax rate from 28 to 21 per cent, intended to improve incentives for R&D investment and innovation.
reforms.package_name: E-business and Venture Capital Tax Incentives
reforms.component_name: Corporate and capital gains tax rate reductions
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Lower corporate and capital gains tax rates reduce the effective tax burden on R&D investment and entrepreneurial returns, improving incentives for private-sector innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'In the October 2000 Budget Update the Minister of Finance announced a further cut in the federal capital-gains-inclusion rate' and 'the timetable for reducing the corporate tax rate...was moved forward'.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant tax policy reform with economy-wide implications for R&D incentives; part of coordinated effort to improve Canada's innovation competitiveness relative to the United States.
reforms.source_quote: In the October 2000 Budget Update the Minister of Finance announced a further cut in the federal capital-gains-inclusion rate, from 67 to 50 per cent...the timetable for reducing the corporate tax rate from 28 to 21 per cent was moved forward.

reforms.description: The government launched a substantial boost to the Canada Foundation for Innovation, a public organisation developing research facilities and networks, as part of the October 2000 Budget Update to stimulate research and innovation.
reforms.package_name: October 2000 Budget R&D and Innovation Initiatives
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Investment in research facilities and networks enhances the physical and institutional infrastructure for scientific research, supporting productivity growth through knowledge creation.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'The October 2000 Budget Update included a variety of measures designed to stimulate research and innovation mainly via a substantial boost to the Canada Foundation for Innovation'.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant investment in research infrastructure supporting Canada's goal to be among OECD's top five R&D performers by 2010; part of broader federal R&D spending increase strategy.
reforms.source_quote: The October 2000 Budget Update included a variety of measures designed to stimulate research and innovation mainly via a substantial boost to the Canada Foundation for Innovation, a public organisation developing research facilities and networks.

reforms.description: The government set an official goal for Canada to be one of the OECD's top five R&D performers by 2010, with an objective to double direct federal R&D spending by that point, supported by multiple initiatives and programmes to fund research.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Doubling public R&D spending increases the knowledge base and research capacity, supporting long-term productivity growth and innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'Canada's official goal is to be one of the OECD's top five R&D performers by 2010. In that perspective, the government has set an objective of doubling direct federal R&D spending by that point'.
reforms.importance_rationale: Structural, system-wide commitment to substantially increase public R&D investment with a clear long-term target; represents major policy shift to address Canada's R&D intensity gap relative to G-7 peers.
reforms.source_quote: Canada's official goal is to be one of the OECD's top five R&D performers by 2010. In that perspective, the government has set an objective of doubling direct federal R&D spending by that point, and...it has launched several initiatives over the years to stimulate investment in R&D.

reforms.description: In March 2001, the Canadian government announced C$750 million in spending on new research and development projects, in addition to C$500 million made available in the October 2000 Budget Update, totalling C$1.25 billion in new R&D funding.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increased public R&D spending enhances the knowledge base and innovation capacity of the economy, supporting long-term productivity and competitiveness.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'In March 2001, the government announced that C$750 million would be spent on new research and development projects. This came in addition to the C$500 million made available in the October 2000 Budget Update,' indicating the October 2000 allocation was already in effect.
reforms.importance_rationale: This represents a substantial increase in federal R&D investment (C$1.25 billion total), a system-wide commitment to research funding that signals structural support for innovation capacity across the economy.
reforms.source_quote: In March 2001, the government announced that C$750 million would be spent on new research and development projects. This came in addition to the C$500 million made available in the October 2000 Budget Update.

reforms.description: The Canada Foundation for Innovation was established as an independent not-for-profit corporation to provide funding to universities, colleges, hospitals and other not-for-profit institutions to obtain necessary research infrastructure. The foundation received C$1.0 billion in federal funding from 1996-97 to 2002-03, with C$1.5 billion in leveraged funding from other sources.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Investment in research infrastructure enhances the capacity of public research institutions to conduct high-quality research, supporting long-term productivity and innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: The foundation was established in 1997 under the Budget Implementation Act 1997 and began providing funding from 1996-97 to 2002-03.
reforms.importance_rationale: This was a major structural reform creating a dedicated national institution for research infrastructure funding. It represented a significant new mechanism for supporting university and hospital research capacity across Canada, with substantial federal and leveraged funding over a multi-year period.
reforms.source_quote: Canada Foundation for Innovation... Independent not-for-profit corporation created under the Budget Implementation Act 1997 to provide funding to universities, colleges, hospitals and other not-for-profit institutions to obtain necessary research infrastructure
